title: Why Carbon Is Special: Hydrocarbons

cards.b: Over 90 percent of known compounds contain carbon. Your body, plastic, petrol, medicines, cotton, silk: all carbon-based. Organic chemistry is the study of carbon compounds. Why one element makes so many compounds is the question here.

• Four bonds: carbon has 4 outer electrons and shares them, forming four covalent bonds.
  • Catenation: carbon atoms bond strongly to each other, forming long chains, branches and rings.
  • Multiple bonds: single, double and triple.
  • Isomers: same formula, different arrangement.

Silicon is below carbon but its chains are weak, so life chose carbon.

Chemists once thought organic compounds needed a 'vital force' from living things. Friedrich Wöhler, 1828, made urea from ammonium cyanate in a flask, a compound of living bodies, from inorganic materials. The vital-force idea faded. August Kekulé (1865) proposed the ring structure of benzene.

Hydrocarbons contain only carbon and hydrogen.

  • Alkanes (single bonds, CnH2n+2): methane CH4, ethane C2H6, propane C3H8, butane C4H10.
  • Alkenes (one C=C, CnH2n): ethene C2H4, propene C3H6.
  • Alkynes (one C≡C, CnH2n-2): ethyne (acetylene) C2H2.
  • Aromatic: benzene C6H6, a stable ring.

Alkanes are 'saturated'; alkenes and alkynes are 'unsaturated'.
The stem tells the chain length: meth 1, eth 2, prop 3, but 4, pent 5, hex 6, hept 7, oct 8. The ending tells the family: -ane (single), -ene (double), -yne (triple).

Butane C4H10 can be arranged as a straight chain (n-butane) or branched (isobutane, or methylpropane). Same formula, different properties. Isomers multiply fast: C10H22 has 75 isomers. This is another reason carbon chemistry is so rich.

• Combustion: complete: hydrocarbon + O2 → CO2 + H2O. Incomplete burning gives CO and soot.
  • Substitution (alkanes): CH4 + Cl2 → CH3Cl + HCl in light.
  • Addition (alkenes): C2H4 + Br2 → C2H4Br2. Decolourising bromine water tests for double bonds.
  • Hydrogenation: C2H4 + H2 → C2H6 with nickel catalyst.

Propane: C3H8 + O2 → CO2 + H2O.

  1. 3 carbons: 3CO2.
  2. 8 hydrogens: 4H2O.
  3. Oxygen on right: 6 + 4 = 10 atoms, so 5O2.

C3H8 + 5O2 → 3CO2 + 4H2O. Burning 44 g (1 mol) propane gives 3 mol CO2 = 132 g. A rule: formula of an alkane with 6 carbons is C6H14 (2 x 6 + 2 = 14).

• Organic does not mean natural or healthy. It just means carbon-based; plastics are organic compounds.
  • Not every carbon compound is organic: CO2, carbonates, and diamond are usually classed as inorganic.
  • Isomers are not the same substance.
  • Saturated does not mean 'full of water'. It means no double bonds.

Digboi in Assam, where oil was struck in 1889 and the refinery began in 1901, is among the oldest operating refineries in the world. Reliance's Jamnagar complex in Gujarat is one of the largest refining sites on Earth. Ethanol, a carbon compound from sugarcane, now blends into petrol under India's E20 programme (20 percent ethanol, rolled out widely by 2025).

• Carbon forms four bonds, long chains, rings and multiple bonds.
  • Alkanes CnH2n+2, alkenes CnH2n, alkynes CnH2n-2.
  • Isomers share formula but differ in structure; combustion makes CO2 and water.

Think about it

1. Why can carbon form millions of compounds while neon forms none?

2. How would you tell hexane from hexene using bromine water?
